As the final days of pregnancy approach, many women feel more anxiety than joy. They stay awake at night, read "scary birth stories" on the internet, and replay the same scenarios in their minds: *"What if I can't do it?", "Will I be able to stand the pain?", "Will something happen to my baby?"*.

Dear future mother, you must know that you are not alone. It is completely normal to be afraid of childbirth. However, if this fear reaches a level that paralyzes your life, it may be a medical condition – **Tokophobia**.

In this article, we will delve into the roots of the fear of childbirth and learn ways to turn this fear into confidence with 5 effective methods recommended by psychologists.What is Tokophobia? Difference from normal anxiety

Every pregnant woman experiences some anxiety regarding the birth process. This is the "fear of the unknown" and it is natural. However, **Tokophobia** is a pathological (extreme) fear.  - **Symptoms:** Panic attacks, nightmares, increased heart rate when thinking about birth, crying spells, and even persistently demanding a cesarean section due to this fear.3 main sources of fear

To face your fear, you must first name it. What do you fear the most?1.  **Fear of pain:** "There will be unbearable pain, I will die".
2.  **Fear of losing control:** "I won't be able to control my body, the doctors won't listen to me".
3.  **Fear of trauma:** "There will be tearing, my health will be ruined".5 Psychological Techniques to overcome fear1. Maintain an "Information Diet"

In our society, women love to tell exaggerated stories of difficult births to prove their "heroism".  - **Advice:** Stop listening to negative stories. When your friend starts with "I was in labor for 20 hours...", politely interrupt her: *"Please, I only need positive stories"*. Feed your brain with successful and calm birth stories, not scary scenarios.2. Use the power of knowledge

Humans fear what they do not know most. Learn the physiology of the birth process.  - **Fact:** A contraction (surge) is not meant to cause pain, but to open the cervix. Every contraction is a "labor force" bringing you closer to your baby.
  - **Action:** Go to birth preparation courses or watch birth videos in the **Anacan app**. Knowing the process step-by-step will give you a sense of control.3. Replace the word "Pain" with "Power" (Hypnobirthing)

Our language shapes our thoughts. Instead of saying to yourself "Unbearable pain is coming", say "A strong wave is coming".  - **Technique:** Instead of tensing your body when a contraction comes (which increases pain), try to relax. Take a deep breath and imagine that with every exhale, the tension in your body flows away into water.4. Build a "Bridge of Trust" with your doctor

Do not hide your fears from your doctor. Tell them, "I am very afraid". A good doctor will take your feelings seriously and calm you down.  - **Discussion:** Discuss pain relief options (Epidural anesthesia) in advance. Knowing that pain can be managed will give you peace of mind.5. Prepare a Birth Plan (But be flexible)

Planning what will happen at the hospital reduces stress.  - Who will be with you? (Your partner, your mother?).
  - Do you want to listen to music?
  - Should the lights be dimmed?
    Thinking about these small details will shift your focus away from fear and toward a sense of "nesting".When is professional help needed?

If your fears interfere with your daily life, disrupt your sleep and appetite, be sure to see a perinatal psychologist. A few sessions of therapy can help untie this knot.

Childbirth is the most natural and powerful function of the female body. Your body is programmed to do this job. Millions of women have succeeded, and you will too.

Fear is normal, but do not let it overshadow the most beautiful day of your life. Take a deep breath, think of your baby, and say to yourself: *"I am strong, I can do this\!"*.

**To calm down:** You can manage your stress throughout pregnancy by using the "Meditation and Breathing Exercises" section in the **Anacan app**.
